 Letter To The Editor 4 hours ago 1 min read Sometimes I wonder how much weight our vote carries after Election Day. Our votes help decide who gets elected, and that matters. But campaigns rely on PACs and donors, and people with money and organized interests can gain more access to lawmakers than ordinary voters. It can leave us wondering whether the people who told us what we wanted to hear during the campaign are still listening once they’re in office. 
 In Congress, moving legislation often requires negotiation and compromise. Lawmakers may have to make deals to get something important done for our state. But we should keep asking whose priorities shape those deals — and whether our communities’ needs are still being heard. 
 Holding elected officials accountable doesn’t mean they have to agree with every voter. It means we keep paying attention, ask questions, follow their votes, and let them know when we agree or expect better. Our vote matters, but our work as citizens doesn’t end on Election Day. 
 Sandra Edwardson 
 Juneau
